reports.title: Detailed processing, source evidence and comparison tutorial
Exact input identities, SHA-256 and native quality audit

question: Can combined HH/HV radar changes recover the published Timber Fire footprint?
method: For each view, average valid native gamma-zero linear powers to the tested 20 m UTM grid. Take the median of its three pre-fire passes. Compute post/baseline log-ratios in HH and HV and add their absolute values. Average the latest valid view magnitudes, normalized-Gaussian smooth (sigma 80 m, minimum support 0.3, missing cells retained), then standardize over the bundled land window by median and 1.4826 MAD. Retain z ≥ 2 and four-connected patches ≥ 10 ha. No unaffected reference rectangle, optical burn labels or official perimeter is used to calculate this score.
expected: Archived single-case evaluation: 7,453.00 ha candidate change on 45,228.56 ha usable land. On 45,208.76 ha of common radar/optical evaluation support, NIFC-perimeter AUC was 0.9862, precision 0.9965, recall 0.7244 and F1 0.8389. Author-outline IoU was 0.9643; that outline uses the same NISAR observations and is not independent ground truth.
interpret: Start with the change score: brighter means stronger unusual radar change within this land window, not higher burn severity. Candidate patches show where the score and area rules are met; zero means the rule was not met, not confirmed unburned. Check view count: one valid view can contribute where the other is missing. Explore time contains two individual-view magnitude frames in dB, not a fused animation; missing dates are unobserved. Advanced maps retain HH/HV directions and unsmoothed/smoothed magnitudes.
limits: Single-fire, provisional-product case study based on a preprint, not universal validation. Static NISAR water masking is replaced by a simplified Sentinel-2 land polygon, and per-view DEM/LOS layover/shadow masks are absent. One native frame per pass covers the extracted study window rather than the authors’ full mosaics. Grid coordinates were inferred from rounded viewer bounds; product revisions and current official perimeter may differ. Radar change is not burn severity or recovery. Only the final primary comparison dates are bundled; intermediate fire-evolution dates were not downloaded.

evidence.label: Quantitative single-case comparison
evidence.description: The strongest numerical example: a real NISAR change mask compared with an official incident boundary, with close author-output agreement. This is a single-case evaluation, not general burn accuracy.
evidence.transfer_validation: Not established on an independently held-out event or region.

comparison_review.conclusion: The strongest numerical example: a real NISAR change mask compared with an official incident boundary, with close author-output agreement. This is a single-case evaluation, not general burn accuracy.
agrees: Fresh radar-support evaluation against the archived official NIFC snapshot reproduces precision 0.9965, recall 0.7244 and F1 0.8389. AUC is 0.98617 on 45,228.56 ha of common finite radar support.

Mapped candidates cover 7,453.00 ha; author-output IoU is 0.9643 on that archived support. The author outline uses the same NISAR observations and is reproducibility evidence, not an independent sensor.
differs: The full study is a preprint, not peer reviewed. Our simplified Sentinel-2 land domain replaces its static water exclusions; no DEM/LOS terrain mask is applied.
The current NIFC snapshot, inferred grid envelope and source revisions can differ. The application’s valid land area and the archived common radar/optical evaluation area have different denominators.
unverified: An incident perimeter is an operational proxy that can include unburned islands; precision here is not a universal burned-pixel accuracy.
No held-out fire/region, field severity validation or recovery series is demonstrated.
comparison_review.next_check: A separate fire with independently sampled burn labels and fixed parameters; terrain-mask and normalization-window sensitivity.
comparison_review.quantity_reference: Study scattering score/candidate mask; official incident perimeter; optical context
comparison_review.quantity_ours: Combined unsigned HH/HV change score · z; candidate patches · ha
comparison_review.support: Fresh evaluation: 45,228.56 ha finite radar support. Archived common radar/optical evaluation: 45,208.76 ha. F1 and mask IoU agree exactly; AUC changes slightly with the denominator. The selected window also sets score normalization.
comparison_review.reason: It has the most inspectable numerical evaluation, archived official/reference boundaries and a clear distinction between algorithm reproduction and independent evidence.
comparison_review.reproducibility: Protected input checksums and unchanged guided/editable replay test implementation reproducibility; they do not test environmental accuracy.
comparison_review.source_review: See docs/EXAMPLE_EVIDENCE_REVIEW.md for source access and archived-evidence limits.

numerical_check.note: Fresh radar-only support, not the historical radar/optical support. Author-output agreement is reproduction evidence.

metric_help: About 99.65% of mapped candidate cells fall inside the official incident perimeter. This does not mean 99.65% of all truly burned pixels were correctly identified.
About 72.44% of the evaluated perimeter interior is mapped as a candidate. The operational perimeter can contain unburned islands, so unmapped interior is not automatically a missed burn.
A balance of precision and recall against that same perimeter. It is not a general accuracy percentage.
How well the continuous radar score ranks cells inside versus outside the reference across thresholds. It is not a burn probability or proof of fire causation.
Intersection divided by union of two masks. Official-boundary and author-output IoU use different references; the author output shares the NISAR inputs and is reproduction evidence.
